newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down on Tuesday on a technical correction after sharp gains on Monday, traders said.
Slight losses on the domestic A share market today also pushed some funds back to the repo market, they said.
The annual rate for the most active 14-day contract fell to 12.90 percent from 16.00 percent.
Turnover fell to 6.48 million lots from 9.11 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The correction on the A share market helped to bring down the repo rates today," one trader said.
"Volume of early-maturing contracts, three-day and seven-day contracts, fell sharply, with many institutions ceasing to borrow today due to a fall on the A market," he added.

But traders believe the early-maturing contracts will rebound in the next few days with more new A share issues and listings, they said. On Wednesday, Shanghai Pudong Stainless Sheet and Haci Co, a maker of magnetic products, will list.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with institutions continuing to sell because of weak market sentiment, traders said. The market has fallen since early this month, with investors expecting low coupons for new T-bills.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 119.37 yuan from 119.79.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.31 million lots from 1.51 million.
Traders said the contracts were unlikely to recover in the short term due to weak investor confidence and an active A share market, which was likely to draw funds from the spot market.
